artifacts.title: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

artifacts.title: PCA v. Gulfstream
artifacts.synopsis: Gulfstream Presbytery was cited and appeared before the SJC regarding exceptions of substance found in its records; the SJC accepted the presbytery's response as acceptable, pending certification that the response was approved by the presbytery.

artifacts.synopsis: The Korean Eastern Presbytery's Administrative Commission exceeded its authority under BCO 13-9 by calling and facilitating a congregational meeting to vote on ruling elders without proper BCO authority, as complaint procedures under BCO 25-2 and 43 should have been followed instead. The SJC sustained the complaint, reaffirming precedents limiting presbytery power and the principle that a higher court may not 'act for' a lower court.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC affirmed KEP's denial of the appeal regarding the underlying guilty verdicts, but sustained the error of increasing the censure from suspension to excommunication and deposition on appeal, holding that appellate courts may not increase censures beyond what the trial court imposed. The case arose from discipline of two ruling elders who refused to recognize the results of a congregational election.

artifacts.title: Scope of presbytery stated clerk's duty to disseminate information

matches.evidence: CCB advised that a stated clerk may provide information consistent with presbytery records, especially when requested by a former TE in connection with ecclesiastical litigation.

artifacts.title: Certification of presbytery dismissal by committee chairman's letter

matches.evidence: A letter from a presbytery committee chairman is insufficient evidence of dismissal; BCO 46-6 requires a certificate bearing the stated clerk's signature per BCO 10-4.
